title: Split an arrow using the given angle
text:
Read and explain

Target S2 Pairs

Split an arrow using the given angle

A **20 N** pull points **30°** above the positive x-axis.

Fx = **20** cos **30°** ≈ **17.3 N**

Fy = **20** sin **30°** = **10.0 N**

Both parts describe the same force. They are not two extra forces.

title: Check the angle before choosing sine or cosine
text:
**2026**-XJ · The Arrow Test · Graphic novel, page **23**

**Check the angle before choosing** sine or cosine

The same arrow is ten meters each second. It is 30 degrees above horizontal, or 60 degrees from vertical. Its parts stay 8.66 across and 5 up. Mr. Antocci says to use cosine for the part beside the marked angle.

An arrow can have angles measured from different axes. It is still the same arrow. Cosine goes with the part next to the angle.

How can two ways of naming the angle give the same two parts?
